results.proposed_proof:
**Given:** Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, the smooth fields, foliation, temporal gauge, reduced equations, and initial compatibility, Maxwell, harmonic, and total-stress Einstein constraints in the Statement.

[L1] [[def-emg-trivial-potential-charged-scalar-system]] fixes $F=dA$, $\pi=D\varphi$, the sourced Maxwell sign $\nabla_aF^{ab}=-\mu_0j^b$, and $T=T^{\mathrm{EM}}+T^\varphi$. These formulas specify the model to be recovered from the reduced equations.

[L2] [[lem-emg-temporal-scalar-positive-symmetric-reduction]] states the temporal-gauge evolution $\partial_s\varphi=\pi_0$, $\partial_sA_i=F_{0i}$, and $\partial_s\pi_i-\partial_i\pi_0=-i\lambda A_i\pi_0-i\lambda F_{0i}\varphi$. These are the actual first-order evolution equations.

[L3] [[lem-emg-charged-scalar-variation]] gives, for $E_\varphi:=D_a\pi^a-V'(|\varphi|^2)\varphi$, the identities $\nabla_aj^a=K_\varphi\lambda\operatorname{Im}(\overline\varphi E_\varphi)$ and $\nabla_a(T^\varphi)^a{}_b=K_\varphi\operatorname{Re}(\overline{E_\varphi}\pi_b)+F_{ba}j^a$. The identities are used only after their field-compatibility hypotheses have been established.

[L4] [[lem-emg-maxwell-stress-divergence]] states that smooth fields satisfying $dF=0$ and $\nabla_aF^{ab}=-\mu_0j^b$ obey $\nabla_aT_{\mathrm{EM}}^{ab}=-F^{bc}j_c$. The identities are used only after their field-compatibility hypotheses have been established.

[L5] [[lem-emg-fieldstrength-positive-symmetric-reduction]] gives the source-free six-component Maxwell principal block, its evolution/constraint split, and positive time matrix. The current term $j$ is an algebraic lower-order source in this use.

[L6] [[lem-emg-coupled-reduced-einstein-evolution]] gives the harmonic metric wave block with algebraic stress coupling, while [[lem-gr-reduced-einstein-principal-part]] gives the first-order metric variables $p_{ab}=\bar\nabla_0g_{ab}$, $q_{abi}=\bar\nabla_i g_{ab}$, the equation $\bar\nabla_0g_{ab}=p_{ab}$, and the relation $\bar\nabla_0q_{abi}-\bar\nabla_ip_{ab}=\mathcal C_{abi}$, where $\mathcal C_{abi}=-\bar R^c{}_{a0i}g_{cb}-\bar R^c{}_{b0i}g_{ac}=[\bar\nabla_0,\bar\nabla_i]g_{ab}$. The metric derivative relations and principal matrices are used at these exact interfaces.

[L7] [[lem-emg-lorentz-hodge-calculus]] gives $({\star_gF})_{ab}=\tfrac12(\mathrm{vol}_g)_{abcd}F^{cd}$ and $d^2=0$.

[L8] [[thm-gr-density-divergence-and-finite-chain-flux]] gives $d(\iota_j\mathrm{vol}_g)=(\nabla_aj^a)\mathrm{vol}_g$ for smooth $j$; the identity follows from the local volume-density formula.

[L9] [[def-gr-harmonic-gauge-and-reduced-equations]] defines $H$ and the reduced Einstein equation. Its stated gauge and reduced-equation conventions are used.

[L10] [[lem-gr-einstein-residual-and-subsidiary-identity]] states that the reduced Einstein residual is $\tfrac12(\nabla_aH_b+\nabla_bH_a-g_{ab}\nabla_cH^c)$ and, when $\nabla^aT_{ab}=0$, $H$ solves $\Box_gH_b+\operatorname{Ric}_{ba}H^a=0$. The displayed identity is used under its stated hypotheses.

[L11] [[thm-gr-constraint-equations-in-normal-frame]] gives $G(n,n)=\tfrac12(R(h)+\tau^2-|K|_h^2)$ and $G(n,Y)=(\operatorname{div}_hK)(Y)-D_Y\tau$ under the stated $K$ convention. The displayed identity is used under its stated hypotheses.

[L12] [[thm-divergence-theorem-for-bounded-piecewise-c-one-domains]] supplies the local integration-by-parts identity on finite piecewise-$C^1$ domains, and [[thm-gronwall-integral-inequality]] supplies uniqueness from a zero initial energy and $E'(t)\le CE(t)$. Only their integration and zero-energy conclusions are used.

[L13] [[lem-gr-periodic-sobolev-embedding]] states $H^s(\mathbb T^3_{2\pi})\hookrightarrow C^m$ when $s-m>3/2$, so $s\ge5$ supplies the classical derivatives used here. The displayed identity is used under its stated hypotheses.

[L14] [[thm-picard-lindelof-local-existence-and-uniqueness]] and [[thm-c1-dependence-of-solutions-on-initial-data]] give the unique local $C^1$ flow of the $C^1$ normal field; transversality to $\Sigma$ gives local flow coordinates.

[A1] The fields and background are smooth; $\lambda$ is real; the range of $|\varphi|^2$ lies in the open domain of $V$; every displayed Maxwell and Einstein equation is assumed only for the reduced evolution until its constraint and gauge recovery is proved.

[A2] Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$; it is required by the cited Sobolev embedding and finite-domain divergence theorem.



**Proof technique:** propagate the first-order compatibility residuals, then the sourced Maxwell residuals, cancel the scalar and electromagnetic stress exchange, and finally solve the Einstein gauge subsidiary with its constraint-determined Cauchy data.

1.1 Differentiate $C_i$ in $s$ and group the compatibility equation from [L2]: $\partial_sC_i=(\partial_s\pi_i-\partial_i\pi_0)+i\lambda(\partial_sA_i)\varphi+i\lambda A_i\partial_s\varphi=(-i\lambda A_i\pi_0-i\lambda F_{0i}\varphi)+i\lambda F_{0i}\varphi+i\lambda A_i\pi_0=0$. Thus $C_i=0$ on the initial slice implies $C_i=0$ throughout the local time region, and the definition of $\pi_i$ in [L1] gives $\pi_i=D_i\varphi$. [given, L1, L2, A1, algebra]

1.2 Let $R_{abi}:=q_{abi}-\bar\nabla_i g_{ab}$. The first-order metric equations in [L6] include $\bar\nabla_0g_{ab}=p_{ab}$ and $\bar\nabla_0q_{abi}-\bar\nabla_i p_{ab}=\mathcal C_{abi}$, where $\mathcal C_{abi}=[\bar\nabla_0,\bar\nabla_i]g_{ab}$. Therefore $\bar\nabla_0R_{abi}=\bar\nabla_i p_{ab}+\mathcal C_{abi}-\bar\nabla_0\bar\nabla_i g_{ab}=\bar\nabla_i\bar\nabla_0g_{ab}+[\bar\nabla_0,\bar\nabla_i]g_{ab}-\bar\nabla_0\bar\nabla_i g_{ab}=0$. The initial metric jet gives $R_{abi}=0$, so the first-order spatial metric variables remain the actual derivatives of $g$. [given, L6, A1, algebra]

1.3 First propagate the magnetic residual $U:=dF$, independently of the scalar equation and current. The normal evolution gives $\iota_nU=0$, so a three-form decomposition in an adapted frame gives $U=q\,\iota_n\mathrm{vol}_g$. Its pullback to the initial slice is $(D_ib^i)\mathrm{vol}_h=0$, hence $q=0$ initially. Since $dU=d^2F=0$, the coordinate volume formula gives $\nabla_a(qn^a)=n(q)+q\nabla_an^a=0$. On each normal integral curve the integrating factor $\exp(\int\nabla_an^a)$ makes $q$ constant times its initial value, so $q=0$ near the initial slice. Thus $dF=0$ before any current-conservation or Einstein inference. The normal is transverse to the time levels and its local flow exists with unique curves; at the stated finite Sobolev regularity it is at least $C^1$. [given, L5, L7, L8, L13, L14, A1, A2, algebra]

2.1 The full closedness now proved gives $\partial_sF_{ij}-\partial_iF_{0j}+\partial_jF_{0i}=0$ in coordinates. Since $\partial_sA_i=F_{0i}$, differentiating $B_{ij}=F_{ij}-(\partial_iA_j-\partial_jA_i)$ gives $\partial_sB_{ij}=0$. Its initial value is zero, so $B_{ij}=0$; also $A_0=0$ gives $F_{0i}=\partial_sA_i-\partial_iA_0$. Consequently every component satisfies $F=dA$. Step 1.1 gives $\pi_i=D_i\varphi$, and $\partial_s\varphi=\pi_0$ with $A_0=0$ gives $\pi_0=D_0\varphi$, so $\pi=D\varphi$ in all slots. The reduced scalar divergence equation is therefore the actual scalar equation $E_\varphi=0$ in [L3]. [given, L1, L2, L3, step 1.1, step 1.3, algebra]

3.1 With $F=dA$, $\pi=D\varphi$, and $E_\varphi=0$, the current and scalar-stress identities in [L3] now give $\nabla_aj^a=0$ and $\nabla_a(T^\varphi)^a{}_b=F_{ba}j^a$. The form/source sign is fixed independently: put $v^b:=\nabla_aF^{ab}$. Metric compatibility preserves the oriented volume and Hodge star, while torsion-freeness identifies exterior differentiation with antisymmetrized covariant differentiation. In a positively oriented orthonormal frame, [L7] gives $(d\star_gF)_{123}=-v^0$ and $(d\star_gF)_{0ij}=\epsilon_{ijk}v^k$; the corresponding components of $\iota_v\mathrm{vol}_g$ are $v^0$ and $-\epsilon_{ijk}v^k$. Hence $d\star_gF=-\iota_v\mathrm{vol}_g$ for any such $F$. In particular, $d\star_gF=\mu_0\iota_j\mathrm{vol}_g$ is equivalent to $v=-\mu_0j$; neither equation is assumed before the residual proof in the next step. [given, L1, L3, L7, step 2.1, algebra]

4.1 Put $W:=d\star_gF-\mu_0\iota_j\mathrm{vol}_g$. Its normal contraction vanishes by the sourced evolution, so $W=r\,\iota_n\mathrm{vol}_g$. Initially, the Hodge formula in [L7] gives $(\star_gF)|_\Sigma=\iota_e\mathrm{vol}_h$, while $(\iota_j\mathrm{vol}_g)|_\Sigma=j^0\mathrm{vol}_h$. Thus $W|_\Sigma=(D_ie^i-\mu_0j^0)\mathrm{vol}_h=0$. By [L8] and step 3.1, $dW=-\mu_0(\nabla_aj^a)\mathrm{vol}_g=0$. The same normal-volume computation as step 1.3 gives $n(r)+r\nabla_an^a=0$ with zero initial value, and the integrating factor proves $r=0$. Thus the full sourced Maxwell equation holds, with the divergence sign established in step 3.1. For the classical finite-Sobolev solutions, these identities also hold distributionally; the continuous residuals and their initial traces give the same zero solution in the $C^1$ normal flow coordinates. [given, L5, L7, L8, L13, A1, A2, step 1.3, step 3.1, algebra]

5.1 Combining the on-shell scalar identity from step 3.1 with [L4] gives $\nabla_aT^{a}{}_b=F_{ba}j^a-F_{ba}j^a=0$, equivalently $\nabla^aT_{ab}=0$ because $T$ is symmetric. This conservation holds before the Einstein equation is recovered. [L1, L3, L4, step 3.1, step 4.1, algebra]

6.1 Let $E_{ab}:=G_{ab}+\Lambda g_{ab}-\kappa T_{ab}$. By [L9]–[L10], $E_{ab}=\tfrac12(\nabla_aH_b+\nabla_bH_a-g_{ab}\nabla_cH^c)$. Since $H|_\Sigma=0$, its tangential covariant derivatives vanish there. In an orthonormal frame $(n,e_i)$, $\nabla_cH^c=-\nabla_nH_n$ on $\Sigma$, so $E(n,n)=\tfrac12\nabla_nH_n$ and $E(n,e_i)=\tfrac12\nabla_nH_i$. The normal Einstein projections in [L11] and the assumed initial constraints set both residual components to zero. Therefore $H$ and its normal derivative vanish on $\Sigma$. [given, L9, L10, L11, step 5.1, algebra]

7.1 The homogeneous wave equation in [L10] is a linear wave system with smooth lower-order curvature coefficients. The inherited inequalities $g^{00}<0$ and $(g^{ij})>0$ hold in the reduced region. In a smaller spacelike coordinate cylinder, write its principal part as $g^{00}\partial_s^2H_b+2g^{0i}\partial_s\partial_iH_b+g^{ij}\partial_i\partial_jH_b$ and introduce $v_b=\partial_sH_b$ and $w_{bi}=\partial_iH_b$. The compatibility equations are $\partial_sw_{bi}-\partial_iv_b=0$; substituting them into the wave equation gives the symmetric matrices of a scalar wave reduction, with time matrix $\operatorname{diag}(-g^{00},(g^{ij}))$ repeated over $b$. Thus the first-order state $Y=(H,v,w)$ has a positive time matrix and symmetric spatial matrices, while connection and curvature terms are bounded zero-order coefficients on a compact cylinder. Choose a ball shrinking at speed $\sigma$ greater than $\sup_{|\xi|=1}\|\xi_iA^i\|/\lambda_{\min}(A^0)$. For $E(s)=\int_{B_{r-\sigma s}}Y^{\mathsf T}A^0Y\,dx$, multiplying the system by $2Y^{\mathsf T}$ and using symmetry gives a divergence identity whose interior terms are bounded by $C E(s)$; the side flux is nonnegative because $\sigma A^0+\nu_iA^i$ is positive definite. The finite-domain divergence theorem [L12] therefore gives $E'(s)\le C E(s)$. The initial data from step 6.1 give $Y=0$ and $E(0)=0$, so Gronwall [L12] yields $E(s)=0$; reverse time for $s<0$. Hence $H=0$ near every initial point, and the reduced equation has $E_{ab}=0$, which is the full Einstein equation. For the stated Sobolev regularity, [L13] supplies the classical derivatives in these identities. [given, L9, L10, L12, L13, A2, step 6.1, algebra] ∎

**Given:** The parameters, smooth potential, finite-Sobolev periodic data or smooth general complete data, and compatibility, constraint, and admissible-state hypotheses in the Statement.

[F1] [[def-emg-trivial-potential-charged-scalar-system]] defines the global real-potential system, exact $F=dA$, charged derivative, current, scalar stress, and Maxwell stress; this is a mathematical system, not a physical postulate.

[L1] [[def-emg-periodic-high-sobolev-state]] defines the real componentwise periodic $H^s$ state class $\mathcal S_s(K,R)$ using the Fourier conventions and $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. Only its stated function-space interface is used.

[L2] [[def-gr-periodic-symmetric-hyperbolic-system]] defines a smooth periodic first-order coefficient family with real symmetric matrices and positive time matrix. Only its coefficient definition is used here.

[L3] [[thm-emg-symmetric-hyperbolic-research-supplier]] gives common-time $H^s$ existence, uniqueness, $H^{s-1}$ stability and smooth persistence for a coefficient family already shown to meet [L2]. Its proof combines the exact periodic existence, uniqueness/stability and smooth-persistence suppliers; the present proof must first verify our blocks.

[L4] [[lem-emg-fixed-smooth-background-harmonic-data]] gives the displayed periodic initial metric jet and $H=0$ for a fixed smooth $\gamma$. The prescribed jet and its regularity are used here.

[L5] [[lem-emg-fieldstrength-positive-symmetric-reduction]] supplies the symmetric Maxwell field-strength principal block; [[lem-emg-coupled-reduced-einstein-evolution]] supplies the harmonic metric block with algebraic stress coupling. Their exact blocks are used with the displayed admissible-metric conditions.

[L6] [[lem-emg-temporal-scalar-positive-symmetric-reduction]] gives the charged scalar block with positive time matrix $\operatorname{diag}(-g^{00},(g^{ij}))$. The displayed coefficient matrices have been computed directly.

[L7] [[lem-emg-charged-scalar-subsidiary-chain]] propagates the metric derivative, scalar, potential, Maxwell, and Einstein-gauge constraints and establishes total-stress conservation before Einstein recovery. Its magnetic, potential, current, electric, stress and gauge recovery order is used here.

[L8] [[def-gr-harmonic-gauge-and-reduced-equations]] gives the trace-reversed reduced equation and harmonic vector. [[lem-gr-reduced-einstein-principal-part]] states that a smooth algebraic stress map leaves the metric principal matrices unchanged. The exact reduced metric operator and algebraic-source property are used.

[L9] [[lem-gr-smooth-composition-and-commutator-estimates]] supplies smooth composition on compact state ranges. [[lem-gr-periodic-sobolev-embedding]] gives $H^s\hookrightarrow C^m$ when $s-m>3/2$, and [[lem-gr-periodic-sobolev-algebra]] gives $H^s$ product control for $s\ge4$. These estimates are applied at the stated integer Sobolev orders and compact state ranges.

[L10] [[thm-gr-constraint-equations-in-normal-frame]] gives the stated normal Einstein projections for $K(X,Y)=g(\nabla_Xn,Y)$. The displayed identity is used under its stated hypotheses.

[L11] [[thm-gr-local-geometric-development]] gives a local-development and data-fixing uniqueness result for complete constrained data of a fixed covariant model whose exact first-order reduction propagates all auxiliaries and whose total stress is conserved before Einstein recovery. It assumes $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ and $\mathrm{DC}$. Its complete-data, covariance and gauge-fixed reduction hypotheses are checked below.

[A1] The periodic state has finite real dimension after splitting complex variables into real and imaginary parts. The admissible open set is chosen so the metric inequalities hold, $|\varphi|^2\in\mathcal U$, and all coefficient maps are smooth with a positive time matrix. No full Axiom of Choice or empirical premise is assumed.



**Proof technique:** verify the complete coupled principal block, apply the stated local Sobolev solver, recover the covariant equations by the subsidiary lemma, then verify the exact geometric-development interface and internal-gauge comparison for general smooth data.

1.1 The prescribed normal/tangential two-form components determine the unique real two-form on $\mathbb R n\oplus T\Sigma$: $F(n,\mathfrak e_i)=-e_i$ and $F(\mathfrak e_i,\mathfrak e_j)=\epsilon_{ijk}b_k$. Exactness $F_\Sigma|_{T\Sigma}=d_\Sigma A_\Sigma$ and $\pi_i=D_i\varphi_0$, together with $\pi_0=\pi_n$ in the initial temporal gauge, make all field and potential entries compatible. The jet in [L4] makes the harmonic vector initially zero. After the fixed invertible rescalings, every component is real and belongs to the stipulated $H^s$ class; the compact range lies in $K_0\Subset K_1\Subset O$. [given, F1, L1, L4, A1, construct]

1.2 On $O$, the metric block has the positive time matrix $\operatorname{diag}(I,-g^{00}I,(g^{ij})I)$ from [L5] and [L8]; the total stress is algebraic in $(g,F,\varphi,\pi)$, so the scalar contribution changes only zero-order terms. The Maxwell block has time matrix $\alpha^{-1}I_6$ and symmetric spatial matrices by [L5]; the sourced current is algebraic in $(g,\varphi,\pi)$ and hence is lower order. The charged scalar block has time matrix $\operatorname{diag}(-g^{00},(g^{ij}))$ on each real and imaginary part by [L6]. The $\varphi$ and $A_i$ transport equations add identity time blocks and zero spatial blocks. These blocks have no off-diagonal derivative couplings, so their direct sum is symmetric with positive time matrix. All coefficient maps are smooth on $O$ by smooth inversion of $g$, smoothness of $V$, and the stipulated open range. [given, F1, L2, L5, L6, L8, A1, algebra]

2.1 Apply [L3] to this verified coefficient family, the state $u_0\in\mathcal S_s(K_0,R)$, and compact sets $K_0\Subset K_1\Subset O$. The solver gives the common interval, values in $K_1$, $L^\infty H^s\cap C H^{s-1}$ state regularity, uniqueness and stability, and smooth persistence for smooth initial data. It asserts only a solution to the reduced first-order system at this step. [given, L1, L2, L3, step 1.1, step 1.2]

3.1 The reduced coefficient system writes $u_s=-(A^0)^{-1}(A^i\partial_i u+B)$ on a compact admissible range. Since $u\in C H^{s-1}$ and the coefficient maps are smooth, the algebra and composition estimates give $u_s\in C H^{s-2}$; differentiating this expression once gives $u_{ss}\in C H^{s-3}$. The metric derivative residual $q_i-\bar\nabla_i g$ satisfies the homogeneous background-commutator ODE and has zero initial value, independently of the matter constraints, so $q_i=\bar\nabla_i g$; also $p=\bar\nabla_0g$ by its evolution. Thus the same Fourier norm and time-derivative argument as for the electrovacuum block gives $g\in L^\infty H^{s+1}\cap C H^s$ and $g\in C^3$ as a spacetime metric at the base order $s=5$: third spatial derivatives come from two spatial derivatives of $q$, mixed third derivatives from spatial derivatives of $p_s$, and third time derivatives from $p_{ss}$, all continuous since $H^2\hookrightarrow C^0$. The algebraic reconstruction of $F$ from $(g,e,b)$ and the scalar component equations likewise give $F,A,\varphi,\pi\in C^2$ where needed. In particular the smooth coordinate time levels have a $C^1$ transverse normal, the normal residual-transport arguments are legitimate, and the subsidiary wave energy has Lipschitz principal coefficients and bounded lower-order coefficients. This verifies the finite-regularity applicability of [L7] before using its conclusion. [given, L5, L6, L7, L9, step 2.1, algebra]

4.1 The initial metric, scalar, potential, and Maxwell compatibilities and all Gauss and Einstein constraints are exactly those of [L7]. Applying that subsidiary result recovers $p=\bar\nabla_0g$, $q_i=\bar\nabla_i g$, $\pi=D\varphi$, $F=dA$, both sourced Maxwell equations, total-stress conservation before Einstein recovery, and $H=0$. Therefore the reduced solution is a full solution of the mathematical system in [F1]. [given, F1, L4, L7, step 2.1, step 3.1]

5.1 Since $q_i=\partial_i g$ up to the fixed smooth background connection, the periodic Fourier norm identity gives $\|g\|_{H^{s+1}}\asymp\|g\|_{H^s}+\sum_i\|\partial_i g\|_{H^s}$; similarly $p=\bar\nabla_0g$ gives the stated time-derivative regularity. From $\pi_i=D_i\varphi$, one has $\partial_i\varphi=\pi_i+i\lambda A_i\varphi$. The $H^s$ algebra estimate in [L9] makes $A_i\varphi\in L^\infty H^s$, and the same estimate in $C H^{s-1}$ gives continuity of the spatial derivatives. The Fourier norm identity $\|f\|_{H^{r+1}}\asymp\|f\|_{H^r}+\sum_i\|\partial_i f\|_{H^r}$ then gives $\varphi\in L^\infty H^{s+1}\cap C H^s$. The field-strength, potential, and $\pi$ regularities are the corresponding components of the reduced state. The embedding in [L9] supplies the classical derivatives needed by the equations at $s\ge5$. [given, L7, L9, step 2.1, step 4.1, algebra]

5.2 For general smooth $\Sigma$, regard $\Psi=(A,\operatorname{Re}\varphi,\operatorname{Im}\varphi)$ as the fixed covariant matter fields; $F=dA$, $\pi=D\varphi$, $j$, and $T$ are the fixed equations and tensorial expressions of [F1]. On each relatively compact initial chart choose a flat comparison metric $\bar g=-(dx^0)^2+\delta_{ij}dx^i dx^j$, set $g_{ij}=h_{ij}$, $g_{00}=-1$, $g_{0i}=0$, $\partial_0g_{ij}=2K_{ij}$, $\partial_0g_{00}=-2\tau$, and $\partial_0g_{0i}=h_{ij}h^{k\ell}\Gamma(h)^j{}_{k\ell}$. The Christoffel formula gives $H^0=\tfrac12\partial_0g_{00}+\tau=0$ and $H^i=-h^{ij}\partial_0g_{0j}+h^{k\ell}\Gamma(h)^i{}_{k\ell}=0$ initially. Set $q_{abi}=\bar\nabla_i g_{ab}$, $p_{ab}=\bar\nabla_0g_{ab}$, reconstruct $F$ from $(e,b)$, and use $\pi_i=D_i\varphi_0$, $\pi_0=\pi_n$, and $A_0=0$. Thus the complete data and all initial auxiliary constraints are specified; $A(n)=0$ fixes the initial temporal gauge. The equations and stress are covariant under local diffeomorphisms because $d$, the metric connection, contractions, and the oriented volume form commute with pullback. Steps 1.2 and 4.1 give the exact smooth symmetric-hyperbolic reduction, propagation of every auxiliary constraint, recovery of the matter equations, and $\nabla^aT_{ab}=0$ before Einstein recovery. The initial constraints are precisely the normal projections in [L10]. These are the explicit reduction, initialization, conservation, and constraint hypotheses of [L11], so the local construction in that theorem gives a development near each initial point; the internal-gauge comparisons and collar patching are verified in steps 6.1–6.1 below. [given, F1, L5, L6, L7, L8, L10, L11, step 1.2, step 4.1, A1]

6.1 (Fix both coordinate and internal gauges before comparison.) Given two smooth developments of the same complete data, use the wave-coordinate construction in [[thm-gr-local-geometric-uniqueness]] on each relatively compact initial ball: solve $\Box_gx^\mu=0$ with $x^0=0$, $x^i=y^i$, $n(x^0)=1$, and $n(x^i)=0$ on the initial surface. Its proof constructs these scalar waves by the same positive symmetric wave reduction and local solver used here, and their initial differential is invertible. The resulting charts are harmonic relative to the same flat comparison metric and have the identical initialized metric jet in step 5.2. A pulled-back potential need not satisfy $A'_0=0$. On each product collar set $\chi(s,x)=-\int_0^s A'_0(\sigma,x)\,d\sigma$ and transform $A'\mapsto A'+d\chi$, $\varphi'\mapsto e^{i\lambda\chi}\varphi'$. Then $A'_0+\partial_s\chi=0$; direct differentiation gives $D_{\!A'+d\chi}(e^{i\lambda\chi}\varphi')=e^{i\lambda\chi}D_{\!A'}\varphi'$, while $F$, current and stress are unchanged. Since $\chi|_\Sigma=0$, tangential initial $A$, $\varphi_0$ and the covariant normal derivative are unchanged. Only after this temporal-gauge restoration do both developments extract to the identical coefficient system of step 1.2 with identical complete initial values. [given, F1, L5, L6, L11, step 1.1, step 1.2, step 5.2, algebra]

7.1 (Local and whole-surface comparison.) On a smaller compact cylinder the two smooth states lie in a common convex admissible neighborhood. Subtract their equations; the coefficient mean-value formula puts their difference $v$ in $A^\mu(u_1)\partial_\mu v+C v=0$, with bounded $C$. If $A^0\ge aI$ and $b\ge\sup_{|\xi|=1}\|\xi_iA^i\|$, choose a shrinking ball with speed $\sigma>b/a$. Symmetry and spatial integration by parts give $E'\le CE$ for $E=\int v^{\mathsf T}A^0v$, since the side-flux matrix $\sigma A^0+\nu_iA^i$ is nonnegative. The zero initial difference gives $v=0$ in both time directions by Gronwall. This is the local coupled energy comparison in [L11], now applied after the internal gauge has actually been fixed. Undoing the gauges gives a local metric isometry and the stated matter-gauge equivalence. Future data-fixing metric isometries have unique germs: their differentials fix tangents and future normals, hence they agree along the normal geodesics from the initial patch. The injective variable-width normal collars and germ-patching construction of [[thm-gr-local-geometric-uniqueness]] therefore yield one metric isometry near the entire initial surface; no uniform width is imposed. For the existence/gluing argument of [L11], choose the common normal product collar and put each local potential into its temporal gauge there, with unchanged initial $A_\Sigma$. On overlaps the local isometry comparisons just proved identify the metrics and $F$; two temporal-gauge potentials with the same initial spatial restriction and same $F$ agree, since their difference has zero time component, zero exterior derivative and zero initial pullback. Their scalar representatives then agree by the same local reduced comparison. Thus the local fields patch on the literal collar, as required for the smooth-development application in step 5.2. [given, F1, L5, L6, L7, L11, step 4.1, step 5.2, step 6.1, algebra]

8.1 (One global real gauge near the initial surface.) Pull the second development back by the metric isometry from step 7.1, and write $B=A_2-A_1$ on a common product collar. The local comparisons give $dB=F_2-F_1=0$, and the common initial data give $B|_{T\Sigma}=0$. Define the global smooth real function $\chi(s,x)=-\int_0^s B_0(\sigma,x)\,d\sigma$. Then $\partial_s(B_i+\partial_i\chi)=\partial_sB_i-\partial_iB_0=0$ and $B_i+\partial_i\chi=0$ initially; also $B_0+\partial_s\chi=0$. Hence $A_2+d\chi=A_1$ on the collar. The local scalar gauge comparisons have this same differential and zero initial value, so their functions agree with $\chi$ and $e^{i\lambda\chi}\varphi_2=\varphi_1$. This gives the asserted global-potential gauge equivalence, with $\chi|_\Sigma=0$, without requiring a nontrivial bundle construction or assuming that a closed one-form on the entire spacetime is exact. [given, F1, L11, step 6.1, step 7.1, algebra] ∎
